diagnosis: The issue lies in the handling of token strings exceeding the buffer size and incorrect state transitions leading to erroneous token processing.

causal_chain: Line 197 checks if `token_ind >= 80`, triggering an error path for long tokens.
Incorrect state handling in `error_or_eof_case` leads to all outputs being errors.
The test cases show that even valid tokens are misclassified, indicating a flaw in the DFA transitions.
mr_refs: MR2: Deleting comments shouldn't affect token counts but does.
MR3: Random comment additions cause unexpected error surges.
MR4: Case insensitivity and comment truncation don't preserve token stats.
MR5: Comment truncation followed by case changes disrupts token processing.
testcase_refs: source_s5_mr2: All outputs are errors despite valid tokens present.
followup_s5_mr2: Same issue after comment line reduction.
source_s1_mr3: Keyword and string not recognized, all errors.

uncertainty: There may be multiple plausible explanations due to the complexity of the DFA and token processing logic, but the buffer size restriction and error handling are primary suspects.
assumption: The buffer size check is too restrictive and causes premature error handling.

edits.rationale: Remove the buffer size restriction to allow longer tokens.
edits.replacement: if(token_ind >= 80) { token_str[token_ind++] = ch; next_st = next_state(cu_state, ch); } else { next_st = next_state(cu_state, ch); }

expected_effect: Allows longer tokens and correct state transitions.
preservation_constraints: Preserve DFA transitions for known keywords and symbols
repair_intent: Fix buffer size restriction causing premature errors.
